title: Transformer Rectifier Unit and Output Bus Bar — Removal

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Removal of a transformer rectifier unit and of the laminated output bus bar assembly behind it, including the isolation sequence and the terminal capping that must be in place before any tool goes into the bay.

sections.purpose: This task removes one transformer rectifier unit and, when required, the output bus bar assembly behind it, so that the unit can be replaced or the bus bar terminal joints can be examined or modified.
sections.job_setup_note: The bay is live until the battery is disconnected, and the bus bar remains at battery potential after ground power is removed. Two people are needed: one at the bay and one at the battery compartment to confirm the isolation. Allow the unit to cool for thirty minutes after any period at full output before touching the case.
sections.procedure: 1. Remove electrical power from the aircraft and put the warning notices at the ground power receptacle and in the flight compartment. 2. Disconnect the battery and cap the terminals. WARNING: THE OUTPUT BUS BAR STAYS AT BATTERY POTENTIAL UNTIL THE BATTERY IS DISCONNECTED AND CAPPED. DO NOT PUT A TOOL INTO THE BAY BEFORE THIS IS DONE. 3. Confirm zero volts at the unit output terminals with a calibrated meter and record the reading. 4. Open the access panels in zone 121 and lift the floor panel in zone 272. 5. Release the contactor 169XU and the circuit breaker 17XU and tag them. 6. Disconnect the input and output connectors at the unit and put protective caps on both. 7. Release the four unit attachment bolts, support the unit and lower it clear. CAUTION: THE UNIT IS HEAVIER THAN IT LOOKS. USE TWO PEOPLE OR A SUPPORT CRADLE. 8. Where the bus bar is also to be removed, release the terminal bolts on the bus bar D2430110204063 in the sequence given in the illustration and keep the Belleville stacks together with their terminals. 9. Disconnect the relay assembly D2430113213358 and remove it with its bracket. 10. Release the ground stud 1GX3 and put an identification tag on the strap. 11. Remove the bus bar assembly and put it on a clean non-conducting surface.
sections.close_out: Put protective caps on every open connector and cover the ground stud face. Record the meter reading, the bolt torques found and any discolouration of the terminal insulation. Do not leave the bay open overnight without a barrier notice at the access panel.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; step 8 applies only to aircraft at the machined bus bar standard

safety_precautions: Put the warning notices at the ground power receptacle.
Disconnect and cap the battery terminals.
Use insulated tools in the bay.
